newsitem.title: UK: Russia to continue mkts liberalisation - C.bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia to continue mkts liberalisation - C.bank.

text.p: Russia will ease restrictions on foreigners investing in its government securities market, making it easier to repatriate profits, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Friday.
"We will continue liberalisation of the domestic securities market," he told a conference on central and eastern European capital markets.
"Foreign investors will be able to convert yields to dollars without limitation," he said, adding that the central bank also planned to move away gradually from the domestic hedging market.

Russian commercial banks at present have to carry out compensatory deals with the central bank, at rates set by the central bank, for currency transactions related to non-resident "S" accounts for Treasury Bills and OFZ government bonds.

Dubinin said the liberalisation programme, announced last year, would be carried out during the rest of this year and the start of next year. The central bank has already published some details of the liberalisation timetable.
"Step by step we will eliminate our participation (as a hedging instrument) in this market," he said. "This is the main idea for liberalisation of this market."
Dubinin described the securities market as an important source of income to cover the budget deficit, attracting about $1 billion in foreign investment per month.
